name: Chateau de Chenonceau
_about: THE CHATEAU DE CHENONCEAU on the Cher (the logis 1514-22, Philibert de l'Orme's bridge 1556-59, Jean Bullant's gallery 1576): the square corps de logis on the piers of the old mill in the river -- white tuffeau, cross windows, four corbelled corner turrets under slate cones, the steep slate roof with its rich lucarnes and tall chimneys, the chapel with its apse and the library on the east front -- the two-storey gallery 60 m across the river on five arches with its oculus dormers, the bridge north to the forecourt island and the Tour des Marques on its moated corner, Diane de Poitiers' and Catherine de Medicis' parterres; the water a pool from OSM's river and canal. Inside: the rib-vaulted vestibule, the rooms either side on both floors, the straight rampe-sur-rampe stair, the chapel, the library, the gallery on both levels (the chequered floor below).
